Precedence for every setting: environment variable > config.json > the

Delete any key you do not want to override; an absent key means 'use the

_comment_admin_passcode: Gates every dataset-changing endpoint: upload, append, column selection,
metadata edits, export, pipeline runs, and dataset deletion. Reading and
asking stay open either way. Set it to null or remove the key to turn the
gate off entirely (the right setting for a single-user desktop install).
Also readable from the ADMIN_PASSCODE environment variable.
_comment_vertex: Which Vertex AI project and region the model calls bill to. Both are
optional and usually absent: the project falls back to the one recorded
by `gcloud auth application-default login`, and the region to the global
endpoint. Set them for a second project or for data residency.
_comment_models: 'default' is the workhorse: induction, labeling, sub-themes, routing —
every stage whose call count scales with the corpus, so hundreds to
thousands of calls per run. 'synth' writes the answer text, one call per
analyst question, and is the one place a pricier model is affordable.
Any model id the Vertex AI endpoint accepts works here. Add a matching
prices_per_mtok entry for it or runs on it will report as unpriced.
_comment_prices_per_mtok: USD per 1,000,000 tokens, as published on the Vertex AI pricing page.
These are merged over the built-in table, so listing a model here
re-prices it and listing an unknown one makes it priceable.
The output rate is charged on thinking tokens too — the app folds them
into output_tokens for exactly that reason, so there is no separate
Per-token rather than per-1M is available in the Settings screen, which
shows both; the file always stores per-1M to match the pricing page.
